passage: Abstract: "when performing cross-validation, these structures are regularly ignored, resulting in serious underestimation of predictive error." and "Block cross-validation, where data are split strategically rather than randomly, can address these issues."
faulty: 10-fold cross-validation with months assigned to folds uniformly at random; a random forest (50 trees, min leaf size 5) predicts abundance from the month's 10 environmental variables; R-squared = 1 - SSE/SST from the pooled held-out predictions. Claim holds when R-squared >= 0.30.
fixed: Forward-in-time blocked evaluation: the 600 months are divided into 10 consecutive blocks; for blocks 3 to 10, the forest is fitted on the months of all earlier blocks only and predicts the block; R-squared is computed from the pooled block predictions (the held-out blocks' own mean as the baseline).
estimand: Faulty: skill at predicting months whose neighbours in time were used for fitting. Fixed: skill at predicting later months from earlier ones.
model_family: Random forest regression (50 trees, min leaf 5). Chosen by me: ROB17's abstract names no model; a flexible non-parametric model is the setting in which interpolation between neighbouring months is easy.
sizes_note: Source sizes: not stated in the abstract (full text not read). 600 months (50 years) x 10 variables = 6k values is a realistic long monitoring series and keeps a check cheap (a few forest fits per evaluation). Dependence of the error on series length: not stated.
exploited_structure: Time order: adjacent months are alike, so a randomly held-out month has neighbours in the fitting data.

structure_statistic.note_value_source: source states none: the abstract gives no autocorrelation; 0.7 is a proposed typical lag-1 autocorrelation of monthly environmental series

notes: Mean lag-1 autocorrelation of the predictors, not of the outcome: unchanged when a claim-false world replaces the outcome. Block count (10 blocks, first two used only as fitting data) fixed by me; the source describes block CV in general.
